pinboard.title: (1) Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO After Affairs: Live Updates - The New York Times
pinboard.description:
Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, according to the company’s board of directors. 

His departure came after revelations that he had extramarital affairs with an executive who reported to him and with a woman whom U.S. intelligence agencies concluded was spying for China.

Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer, will serve as interim chief executive while the search for a permanent replacement is carried out. 

“Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world,” the company’s board said in a statement. “The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.”

Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the advanced chips that are an essential component of artificial intelligence projects. 

U.S. officials suspect that Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where Ms. Huang was a top executive, has helped smuggle restricted chips into China.

Mr. Huang’s departure could affect the economy more broadly. Nvidia has been central to the artificial intelligence boom, a crucial driver of U.S. economic growth while some other sectors have been struggling.

Few tech executives have has as much sway with Mr. Trump.

pinboard.title: IceWM | Window Manager
pinboard.description: IceWM is a window manager for the X Window System. The goal of IceWM is speed, simplicity, and not getting in the user’s way. It comes with a taskbar with pager, global and per-window keybindings and a dynamic menu system. Application windows can be managed by keyboard and mouse. Windows can be iconified to the taskbar, to the tray, to the desktop or be made hidden. They are controllable by a quick switch window (Alt+Tab) and in a window list. A handful of configurable focus models are menu-selectable. Setups with multiple monitors are supported by RandR and Xinerama. IceWM is very configurable, themable and well documented. It includes an optional external background wallpaper manager with transparency support, a simple session manager and a system tray. IceWM is available on popular Linux distributions like Debian, Ubuntu, Arch, OpenSUSE, Gentoo, Slackware, CentOS and also compiles on most *BSDs.
